questiontext:
Integrate {{CT:0}} with respect to \(t\) using the method of integration by parts.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
To solve this problem we will have to use the method of integration by parts
<hint>calc_int_methods_parts</hint>
two times as follows:

Let \(u = {{CT:1}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:2}}dt\) so that
\(du = {{CT:3}}dt\) and \(v = {{CT:4}}\).

Then,
\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:5}} dt &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int u dt \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  uv - \int v du \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:1}}{{CT:4}} - \int {{CT:4}} {{CT:3}} dt + c \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:6}} - \int {{CT:4}} {{CT:3}} dt + c
 \end{array}\]

Now, define \(u = {{CT:3}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:4}}dt\)
so that  \(du = {{CT:7}}dt\) and \(v = {{CT:8}}\).

Then,
\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
\int {{CT:4}}{{CT:3}}dt &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int u dt \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  uv - \int v du \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:3}}{{CT:8}} - \int {{CT:8}} [{{CT:7}}dt] \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:9}} + \int {{CT:10}}dt.
 \end{array}\]

And so
\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
\int {{CT:5}} dt &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:6}} - \left[{{CT:9}} + \int {{CT:10}} d{{CT:11}}\right] + c \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:6}} - {{CT:9}} - \int {{CT:10}} dt + c.
 \end{array}\]
Hence,
\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
2\int {{CT:5}} dt &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:12}} + c \\

\end{array}\]
